authorization_policy_operation_type.description: Provide the operation type of the authorization policy. Allowed values: add authorization policy, modify authorization policy, delete authorization policy, query authorization policy.
authorization_policy_operation_type.x-a2at-value-constraint: Allowed values: add authorization policy, modify authorization policy, delete authorization policy, query authorization policy. When the input contains an allowed value itself or its abbreviation (e.g., "add", "modify", "delete", "query"), map it directly to the corresponding allowed value. Recognized synonym pairs are limited to: create/new/append→add authorization policy, update/edit/change to/adjust to→modify authorization policy, remove/take away/clear→delete authorization policy, view/retrieve/search/find/look up→query authorization policy. Any other verbs not in this list (e.g., export, import, sync, copy, migrate, suspend, approve, archive, download, backup) are out of range and must not be mapped to any allowed value.

network_operation_authorization_policy_l.description: Provide the network operation authorization policy list. Each entry starts with an Arabic number followed by '.' (increasing consecutively from 1); within an entry, each field is expressed as 'field name is value' and separated by commas; multiple entries are each on their own line (separated by newlines).
examples:
1. business scenario is service complaint diagnosis, handling type is service recovery, operation name is tunnel optimization, validity period is 2026-06-01~2030-06-18
2. business scenario is carrier scheduling, handling type is service recovery, operation name is carrier scheduling, validity period is permanently valid
1. policy identifier is 7d8c7b00-3c8c-4f8e-9b1e-9b17b6a3e5c3, validity period is 2026-06-01~2030-06-18
1. business scenario is service complaint diagnosis
network_operation_authorization_policy_l.x-a2at-value-constraint: List text form. Content composition: policy identifier (UUID unique identifier), business scenario, handling type, operation name, validity period. Each entry starts with a number followed by '.' (e.g., '1.'), with numbers increasing consecutively from 1; within an entry, each field is expressed as 'field name is value', with multiple fields separated by commas; multiple entries are each on their own line (separated by newlines). The field names are fixed as follows: business scenario, handling type, operation name, validity period (add form); policy identifier, validity period (modify form); policy identifier (delete form; each delete entry must provide the policy identifier, one or multiple entries supported); query conditions use only the fields actually referenced (e.g., business scenario, handling type). The validity period is a date range (common date notations are acceptable, timestamps not required, date notations may differ across entries within the same list, date values must be real and valid) or "permanently valid"; both are valid. add authorization policy: required; each entry must contain 'business scenario is X, handling type is Y, operation name is Z, validity period is V' (in this order) — four fields in total, no policy identifier needed; the validity period must be a complete range or "permanently valid"; a single date alone is treated as an incomplete range; field values must be meaningful business content, and meaningless characters (e.g., xxx, ###) constitute a format error. modify authorization policy: the entry format is '1. policy identifier is X, validity period is V' (policy identifier first, validity period second); an entry may also contain only the validity period (e.g., '1. validity period is V', treated as batch modification, equally valid); when the validity period can be determined directly from the modification description, prefer the concise form '1. policy identifier is X, validity period is V' (e.g., "1. policy identifier is 7d8c7b00-3c8c-4f8e-9b1e-9b17b6a3e5c3, validity period is permanently valid"); only when the description is too complex to simplify, keep the combination of a policy identifier and a natural-language modification description (e.g., "1. policy identifier is 7d8c7b00-3c8c-4f8e-9b1e-9b17b6a3e5c3, validity period changed to permanently valid") or a natural-language modification description alone (e.g., "1. validity period changed to 2026-01-01~2028-12-31", equally valid); the validity period may be a date range, a single date, or "permanently valid"; only the validity period can be modified, and modification intents on other fields are invalid; an entry with only a policy identifier and no validity period or modification description is an invalid modification request. delete authorization policy: the entry is '1. policy identifier is X'; a condition-style description is also valid (e.g., '1. handling type is service recovery', '1. business scenario is service complaint diagnosis', treated as deleting by filtering on that condition). query authorization policy: optional; not providing this parameter is fully valid; query conditions may be one or more values of business scenario, handling type, or operation name, no complete entry format required. Query conditions must carry field labels in the form 'field name is value' (e.g., 'business scenario is signal coverage optimization'); multiple conditions are separated by commas, and multiple condition groups are numbered, each on its own line. A query condition value is valid by default; it is treated as nonexistent only when the value itself declares nonexistence (e.g., contains self-declared-nonexistent wording such as "nonexistent" — for example "nonexistent scenario XYZ") or is meaningless characters. When an explicit policy identifier appears but is not in UUID format, the policy cannot be located.
